findings.issue_text: [Critical/bug] pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12-22 — All `DB` methods (`TablesList`, `RunCommands`, `QueryFramesInto`) are stubs returning `errors.New("not implemented")`, and the working `go-duck` engine is removed from go.mod, so `SQLCommand.Execute` (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:95-99) and `sql.TablesList` (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23) can never succeed; the feature's entire functionality is deleted with no replacement

[Critical/bug] pkg/expr/reader.go:129-132 — The new gate in `ReadQuery`'s `QueryTypeSQL` case always fires because `enableSqlExpressions` always returns `false`, so every SQL expression query is rejected with an error — a regression from the previous ungated path that parsed these queries successfully

[High/bug] pkg/expr/reader.go:194-200 — `enableSqlExpressions` is dead/inverted logic: `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` inverts the flag, and both the `if enabled` branch and the fallthrough `return false` mean the flag evaluation is discarded and the function can never return `true` (presumably intended: `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`)

[High/test_gap] No test files are touched: existing tests that exercise SQL command execution/`TablesList` (e.g., pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go) will now fail against the always-erroring stub and break CI; they needed to be updated, removed, or gated

[Medium/test_gap] The newly added code paths — `enableSqlExpressions`, the `QueryTypeSQL` rejection in `ReadQuery`, and the stub `DB` — have no unit tests; a basic test of the flag gate would have caught the always-`false` bug in item 3

[Medium/bug] pkg/expr/sql_command.go:95 — the diff calls `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` but only removes the `go-duck` import and never adds `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/expr/sql` to the import block; since Go rejects unused imports, the file only compiles if that package was already imported and used elsewhere — verify the build (same check applies to any other files still importing `go-duck`)

[Low/doc_defect] pkg/expr/reader.go:131 — the error text "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is misleading: this is a feature-toggle check, not an implementation check, and gives users no actionable information (that a flag exists, that the engine was removed, or that the feature is disabled); it should state the actual condition, e.g. "SQL expressions are disabled"

[Low/api] pkg/expr/sql/db.go:24-26 — `NewInMemoryDB()` keeps the exported name and signatures of the removed `duck.NewInMemoryDB` while returning an object on which every operation fails, breaking the API's implied contract; the stubs also return bare `errors.New("not implemented")` with no exported sentinel (e.g., `ErrNotImplemented`), so callers cannot distinguish an unsupported build from a genuine query failure

[Low/doc_defect] This PR converts a previously working feature into one that always errors (a user-facing breaking change) but ships no changelog/release-note entry documenting the removal of the `go-duck` engine and the new failure mode

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `enableSqlExpressions` in `pkg/expr/reader.go`, and it unconditionally returns `false`: it sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, then `if enabled { return false }`, and finally `return false`. This means `enableSqlExpressions` can never return `true`, so the new guard in `ReadQuery` (`if !enabled { return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") }`) will always error for `QueryTypeSQL`, regardless of the feature flag state. The finding correctly identifies dead/inverted logic based on the shown code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the previous DuckDB-backed implementation (`github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck`) with a new `pkg/expr/sql` `DB` stub whose methods always return `errors.New("not implemented")` (TablesList/RunCommands/QueryFramesInto in `pkg/expr/sql/db.go`). Call sites were updated to use this stub: `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` now calls `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands(...)`, and `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` now calls `sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto(...)`, so these operations will now deterministically error if exercised. While the existence of specific tests/CI failures isn't shown in the diff, the always-erroring behavior is a concrete regression/defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] The newly added code paths — `enableSqlExpressions`, the `QueryTypeSQL` rejection in `ReadQuery`, and the stub `DB` — have no unit tests; a basic test of the flag gate would have caught the always-`false` bug in item 3

adjudication.rationale:
The diff introduces `enableSqlExpressions` in `pkg/expr/reader.go`, but it returns `false` on every path:
```go
enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)
if enabled { return false }
return false
```
`ReadQuery` now gates `QueryTypeSQL` on this function and rejects when `!enabled`, so SQL queries will always error with `sqlExpressions is not implemented`, regardless of the flag state. The finding’s note that a basic flag-gate unit test would catch this is consistent with the always-false implementation, even though the diff itself doesn’t show tests.

Since Go requires an import for the `sql.` qualifier, this change as shown would cause a compile error (undefined `sql` or missing import).

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go (QueryTypeSQL case) the code gates SQL parsing on `enabled := enableSqlExpressions(h)` and errors when it’s false. That condition is clearly intended to be a feature-flag check (`h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` inside enableSqlExpressions), so returning `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` is misleading compared to the actual reason (feature disabled / flag not enabled).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] pkg/expr/sql/db.go:24-26 — `NewInMemoryDB()` keeps the exported name and signatures of the removed `duck.NewInMemoryDB` while returning an object on which every operation fails, breaking the API's implied contract; the stubs also return bare `errors.New("not implemented")` with no exported sentinel (e.g., `ErrNotImplemented`), so callers cannot distinguish an unsupported build from a genuine query failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the previously working DuckDB-backed implementation with a new `pkg/expr/sql.DB` whose methods (`RunCommands`, `QueryFramesInto`, etc.) unconditionally return `errors.New("not implemented")` (pkg/expr/sql/db.go), while call sites were updated to construct this DB (`NewInMemoryDB()` in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go and `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` in pkg/expr/sql_command.go). This makes `TablesList()` and SQL execution paths fail at runtime if reached. The point about lacking a sentinel error is valid but secondary; the primary issue is the introduced always-failing behavior behind an exported constructor that is now used by production code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] This PR converts a previously working feature into one that always errors (a user-facing breaking change) but ships no changelog/release-note entry documenting the removal of the `go-duck` engine and the new failure mode

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes SQL expressions non-functional in a verifiable way: `ReadQuery` now gates `QueryTypeSQL` on `enableSqlExpressions(h)`, but `enableSqlExpressions` always returns `false` (it returns `false` in both the `if enabled` branch and the final return), so `ReadQuery` will always return `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. Additionally, the new `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` `NewInMemoryDB()` returns a `DB` whose `RunCommands`/`QueryFramesInto`/`TablesList` are all stubbed with `errors.New("not implemented")`, and call sites (`sql_command.go`, `parser.go`) now rely on this stub. The claim about missing changelog/release note cannot be verified from the provided diff, but the user-facing breakage (always error / not implemented) is directly shown.
